h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר י״ט Pesach — Maamar Yud Tes

p: יוֹם שֵׁנִי
Second Day
קוֹרִין בְּיוֹם זֶה פָּרָשַׁת "שׁוֹר אוֹ כֶשֶׂב"
We read on this day [in the Torah] the section of "An ox or a sheep"
(מְגִילָּה ל"א.),
(Megillah 31a),
וְכֵן בְּסוּכּוֹת.
and likewise on Sukkos.
וְהִנֵּה בְּפָרָשַׁת סוּכּוֹת יֵשׁ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר פְּסוּקִים לְאַרְבָּעָה גַּבְרֵי,
Now in the section of Sukkos there are twelve verses for four men called to the Torah,
וְהָיוּ יְכוֹלִים לְהוֹסִיף פָּרָשַׁת יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים לְפָנָיו, שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לְסוּכּוֹת,
and they could have added the section of Yom Kippur before it, which has a direct connection to Sukkos,
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
based on what they said
(וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כ"א, ד'):
(Vayikra Rabbah 21:4):
יִשְׁעִי בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים וּגְמַר הַיְּשׁוּעָה בְּסוּכּוֹת,
"My salvation begins on Yom Kippur, and the completion of the salvation is on Sukkos,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
as they said
מַאן דְּנָצַח נָקֵט בָּאִין,
"The victor holds the palm branch (bayin),"
וְהָיָה דַּי לִקְרוֹת חֲמִשָּׁה גַּבְרֵי;
which would have sufficed for five men to read;
אוֹ יוֹתֵר יִתָּכֵן לְהוֹסִיף פָּרָשַׁת הַמְּנוֹרָה שֶׁמַּדְלִיקִין בְּכָל יוֹם,
or even better, they could have added the section of the Menorah, which is kindled every day,

וּכְשֶׁחָל בְּשַׁבָּת הָיוּ יְכוֹלִין גַּם כֵּן לְהוֹסִיף פָּרָשַׁת בָּזִיכִין לְאַחֲרָיו שֶׁהוּא בְּשַׁבָּת, וּפָרָשַׁת יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים לְפָנָיו שֶׁשַּׁיָּיךְ לְסוּכּוֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ, וְהָיָה דַּי לִקְרִיאַת שִׁבְעָה גַּבְרֵי!

and when it fell on Shabbos they could also have added the section of the frankincense spoons afterward (which pertains to Shabbos) and the section of Yom Kippur before it (which pertains to Sukkos, as we said), which would have sufficed for the reading of seven men!
וְלָמָּה מַתְחִילִין בְּסוּכּוֹת פָּרָשַׁת "שׁוֹר אוֹ כֶשֶׂב"?
Why, then, do we begin on Sukkos with the section of "An ox or a sheep"?
וּבְרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ מָצִינוּ בַּגְּמָרָא
After all, on Rosh Chodesh we find in the Gemara
(Megillah 22a):
דּוֹלֵג וְאֶמְצָעִי דּוֹלְגָן,
"He skips, and the middle reader repeats,"
וְלֹא הוֹסִיפוּ מִלְּפָנָיו אוֹ מִלְּאַחֲרָיו בְּפָרָשָׁה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ שַׁיָּיכוּת לִקְדוּשַּׁת הַיּוֹם!
and they did not add verses from before or after in a section unrelated to the holiness of the day!
וְאֶפְשָׁר מַה שֶּׁמַּתְחִילִין בְּפָרָשַׁת "שׁוֹר אוֹ כֶשֶׂב" מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא הַקְדָּמָה לְפָרָשַׁת מוֹעֲדוֹת שֶׁהֵם מִקְרָא קֹדֶשׁ דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשִׁי לְהוּ דְּקָבְעִי שְׁנֵי וְיַרְחֵי,

Perhaps the reason they begin with "An ox or a sheep" is because it serves as an introduction to the section of the festivals—which are "holy convocations" that Israel sanctify by fixing years and months,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּפְסָחִים
as they said in Pesachim
(קי"ז:)
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
based on what they said
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה ט"ו, כ"ד):
(Shemos Rabbah 15:24):
כְּלִי חוֹל כְּשֶׁמִּתְמַלֵּא מִן קֹדֶשׁ מִתְקַדֶּשֶׁת, עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם קְדוֹשִׁים וּמְקַדְּשִׁים אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ וְכוּלֵּי
"If a mundane vessel becomes sanctified when filled with something holy, how much more so Israel, who are holy and sanctify the month, etc."
וְזֶה שֶׁהִקְדִּימוּ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ:
and thus they prefaced it with what is written in this section:
וְנִקְדַּשְׁתִּי בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲנִי ה' מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם הַמּוֹצִיא אֶתְכֶם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם וְגוֹמֵר,
"And I shall be sanctified among the Children of Israel; I am Hashem Who sanctifies you, Who brings you out of the land of Egypt, etc.,"
שֶׁבִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם נֶאֱמַר פָּרָשַׁת: הַחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה לָכֶם רֹאשׁ חֳדָשִׁים
for at the Exodus from Egypt was spoken the section "This month shall be unto you the head of months"
לָכֶם הַיְינוּ לְמֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן שֶׁהֵם מְקַדְּשִׁים הַחֹדֶשׁ וּמַכְנִיסִים הַקְּדוּשָּׁה לִכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
"unto you" meaning to Moshe and Aharon, who sanctify the month and infuse holiness into all of Israel,
וְעַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
and according to what they said
(רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כ"ד.):
(Rosh Hashanah 24a):
רֹאשׁ בֵּית דִּין אוֹמֵר מְקוּדָּשׁ וְכָל הָעָם עוֹנִין אַחֲרָיו מְקוּדָּשׁ מְקוּדָּשׁ.
"The head of the court says 'It is sanctified,' and all the people answer after him 'It is sanctified, it is sanctified.'"
אַךְ בְּפֶסַח קָשֶׁה: הָא בְּפָרָשַׁת "שׁוֹר אוֹ כֶשֶׂב" יֵשׁ שְׁמוֹנָה פְּסוּקִים לִתְרֵי גַּבְרֵי,
However, on Pesach there is a difficulty: in the section of "An ox or a sheep" there are eight verses for two men,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ עַד "וּסְפַרְתֶּם" יֵשׁ בּוֹ דַּי לִקְרוֹת לִשְׁלֹשָׁה גַּבְרֵי,
and afterward until "And you shall count" [the Omer] there are enough verses for three men,
וּבִפְרָט אִם יוֹסִיפוּ גַּם פָּרָשַׁת "וּסְפַרְתֶּם" שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ גַּם כֵּן שַׁיָּיכוּת לְפֶסַח, וְיִהְיֶה דַּי לִקְרוֹת לַחֲמִשָּׁה גַּבְרֵי וְאַף לְשִׁבְעָה גַּבְרֵי
and especially if they also add the section of "And you shall count" which directly pertains to Pesach, there would be enough to read for five men and even for seven men [on Shabbos]
וְלָמָּה קוֹרִין בְּפֶסַח פָּרָשַׁת רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים וְסוּכּוֹת?
so why do we read on Pesach the sections of Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, and Sukkos as well?
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן: כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
However, the explanation is as they said
(Rosh Hashanah 2a):
בְּאֶחָד בְּנִיסָן רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לָרְגָלִים.
"On the first of Nisan is the New Year for the pilgrimage festivals."
וְלָמָּה לֹא אָמַר פֶּסַח רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לָרְגָלִים?
Now why did it not say that Pesach is the New Year for the festivals?
וְאָמַרְנוּ שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת אֶחָד בְּנִיסָן רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ, רֹאשׁ שֶׁל הַחֹדֶשׁ, וּבָתַר רֵישָׁא גּוּפָא אָזֵיל
And we explained that in truth the first of Nisan is Rosh Chodesh, the head of the month, and the body follows the head
(עֵירוּבִין מ"א.),
(Eruvin 41a),
שֶׁכּוֹלֵל קְדוּשַּׁת כָּל הַחֹדֶשׁ וְהֶחָג שֶׁבּוֹ,
so that it encompasses the holiness of the entire month and the festival within it;
וְהוּא רֹאשׁ חֳדָשִׁים שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל קְדוּשַּׁת הַמּוֹעֲדוֹת שֶׁכּוּלָּם תְּלוּיִם בְּפֶסַח וְסוּכּוֹת:
and it is "the head of months," encompassing the holiness of all the appointed times, all of which depend on Pesach and Sukkos:
פֶּסַח הַתְחָלַת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְכוֹלֵל גַּם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה תַּכְלִית יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר

Pesach is the initiation of holiness from the side of Hashem, may He be blessed, and it also encompasses the Giving of the Torah, which was the ultimate purpose of the Exodus from Egypt, as it is said
(שְׁמוֹת ג', י"ב):
(Shemos 3:12):
בְּהוֹצִיאֲךָ אֶת הָעָם וְגוֹמֵר תַּעַבְדוּן אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים עַל הָהָר הַזֶּה,
"When you bring the people out, etc., you shall serve God upon this mountain,"
אַךְ נִצְרַךְ לִסְפּוֹר שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים שֶׁבַע לִהְיוֹת מְזוּקָּק שִׁבְעָתַיִם;
except that it was necessary to count seven times seven in order to be refined sevenfold;
וְאִילּוּ הָיָה כְּתִיקּוּנוֹ הָיָה תֵּיכֶף מַתַּן תּוֹרָה וְכָל הַתּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ לֶעָתִיד,
for had the world been in its rectified state, the Giving of the Torah and the entire Torah as it will be in the future would have come immediately,
אַךְ אַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל הוּצְרְכוּ לְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, "רֹב חָכְמָה" לְתַקֵּן הָ"רֹב כַּעַס".
but after the sin they required the Oral Torah, "abundance of wisdom" to rectify "abundance of anger."
וְאִיתָא בְּתִיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר
And it is stated in Tikkunei Zohar
(תִּיקּוּן ל"ו):
(Tikkun 36):
יְהִי אוֹר — דָּא פֶּסַח, וַיְהִי אוֹר — דָּא רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, הֲוָויַת הָאוֹר;
"'Let there be light'—this is Pesach; 'and there was light'—this is Rosh Hashanah, the actualization of the light";
וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים יוֹם שֶׁנִּיתְּנוּ בּוֹ לוּחוֹת אַחֲרוֹנוֹת שֶׁכּוֹלְלִים גַּם מִדְרָשׁ הֲלָכוֹת וְאַגָּדוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה
and Yom Kippur is the day on which the Second Tablets were given, which also include Midrash, halachos, and aggados, as they said in Shemos Rabbah
(מ"ו, א' מ"ז, ז'),
וּפֶסַח כּוֹלֵל גַּם קְדוּשַּׁת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, שֶׁמִּטַּעַם זֶה מְבָרְכִים טַל שֶׁהִיא טַלָּא דְּעַתִּיקָא, תִּזַּל כַּטַּל אִמְרָתִי
and Pesach also includes the holiness of the Oral Torah, which is why we recite the prayer for dew, representing the Dew of Atika, "May my utterance distill like the dew"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים);
(as explained many times);
וְסוּכּוֹת הַגְּמָר מִכָּל הַמּוֹעֲדוֹת: שְׁמִינִי עֲצֶרֶת נְבִיעוּ דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בְּתִיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר
and Sukkos is the culmination of all the festivals: Shemini Atzeres is the wellspring of Torah, as brought in Tikkunei Zohar
(תִּיקּוּן י"ג),
(Tikkun 13),
וְהִיא הַגְּמָר מִקְּדוּשַּׁת פֶּסַח וְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְשָׁבוּעוֹת,
being the culmination of the holiness of Pesach, Rosh Hashanah, and Shavuos;
וּבְהוֹשַׁעְנָא רַבָּה הַגְּמָר מִיּוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, דְּאִיתָא בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה: יִשְׁעִי בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
and on Hoshana Rabbah is the culmination of Yom Kippur, as stated in Midrash Rabbah, "My salvation begins on Yom Kippur,"
וְכָל הֶחָג שׁוֹאֲגִים הוֹשַׁעְנָא, וּבָאַחֲרוֹן הוֹשַׁעְנָא רַבָּה, יְשׁוּעָה גְּדוֹלָה—זֶהוּ הַגְּמָר מִיּוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, וְנִמְסָרִין אָז הַפִּתְקִין מֵרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.

and throughout the festival they cry out Hoshana, and on the final day it is Hoshana Rabbah, "Great Salvation"—this is the completion of Yom Kippur, when the verdicts from Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur are delivered.
וּבְמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה
And in Midrash Rabbah
(וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כ"ז, ח'):
(Vayikra Rabbah 27:8):
"שׁוֹר" — רֹאשׁ לְכָל הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת שֶׁמּוּצָּלִים מִפְּגַם הָעֵגֶל,
"'An ox'—head of all sacrifices, so that they be rescued from the blemish of the Golden Calf"
וְהַיְינוּ עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ אַחַר כָּךְ:
and this follows what they said afterward:
"שׁוֹר" — בִּזְכוּת אַבְרָהָם,
"'An ox'—in the merit of Avraham,"
שֶׁאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ רָצָה לְהַכְנִיס כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ תַּחַת כַּנְפֵי הַשְּׁכִינָה,
for our father Avraham desired to bring the entire world under the wings of the Divine Presence,
וְכֵן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ קִיבֵּל הָעֵרֶב רַב וְהֵם עָשׂוּ הָעֵגֶל
and similarly Moshe Rabbeinu accepted the Mixed Multitude, who made the Golden Calf
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה מ"ב, ו'),
(Shemos Rabbah 42:6),
וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן מִמִּדַּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ, וְיִשְׂרָאֵל מוּצָּלִים מֵאוֹתוֹ עִנְיָן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
and this too stemmed from the attribute of our father Avraham, while Israel are absolved from that sin, as it is said
(שְׁמוֹת ל"ב, ז'):
(Shemos 32:7):
כִּי שִׁחֵת עַמְּךָ
"For your people [the Mixed Multitude] have acted corruptly"
וְלֹא יִשְׂרָאֵל;
and not Israel;
אוֹ "כֶּבֶשׂ" — יִשְׂרָאֵל נִמְשָׁכִין אַחַר ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּצֹאן,
or "'a sheep'—Israel are drawn after Hashem, may He be blessed, like sheep,"
וְכֵן בַּפָּסוּק כְּתִיב
and so in the verse it is written
(יְחֶזְקֵאל ל"ד, ל"א):
(Yechezkel 34:31):
וְאַתֵּן צֹאנִי צֹאן מַרְעִיתִי אָדָם אַתֶּם,
"And you are My sheep, the sheep of My pasture; you are Adam,"
וּבְיִצְחָק כְּתִיב
and regarding Yitzchak it is written
(בְּרֵאשִׁית כ"ב, ח'):
(Bereishis 22:8):
אֱלֹהִים יִרְאֶה לּוֹ הַשֶּׂה לְעֹלָה בְּנִי,
"God will provide for Himself the lamb for a burnt-offering, my son,"
וְכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל מוּכָן לְהַקְרִיב אֶת עַצְמוֹ אִם יַעֲלֶה הָרָצוֹן לִפְנֵי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְנִתְקַן כָּל הַפְּגָם;
for every single Jew is ready to offer himself up if such be the will before Hashem, may He be blessed, and thus the entire blemish is rectified;
אוֹ "עֵז" — בִּזְכוּת יַעֲקֹב, דִּכְתִיב
or "'a goat'—in the merit of Yaakov, as it is written
(Bereishis 27:9):
וְקַח לִי מִשָּׁם שְׁנֵי גְּדָיֵי עִזִּים טֹבִים,
"And fetch for me from there two choice kids of the goats,"
וְאִיתָא בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה
and it is stated in Bereishis Rabbah
(ס"ה, י"ד):
טוֹבִים לְךָ וְטוֹבִים לְבָנֶיךָ וְכוּלֵּי
"Good for you and good for your children, etc."
שֶׁמִּתְכַּפֵּר בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, וּכְתִיב
which atones on Yom Kippur, as it is written
(וַיִּקְרָא ט"ז, כ"ב):
(Vayikra 16:22):
וְנָשָׂא הַשָּׂעִיר — זֶה עֵשָׂו — אֶת כָּל עֲוֹנֹתָם — עֲוֹנוֹת תָּם, יַעֲקֹב אִישׁ תָּם
"And the goat—this is Esav—shall bear upon itself all their iniquities—the iniquities of the 'wholesome man' (tam), Yaakov, a wholesome man"
(מִדְרָשׁ שָׁם, ט"ו).
(Midrash ibid., 15).
וְזֶהוּ גְּמַר קְדוּשַּׁת הַפֶּסַח: כְּשֶׁנִּתְקַן פְּגַם הָעֵגֶל נִגְמַר תַּכְלִית יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם לִזְכּוֹת לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה, קְדוּשַּׁת לוּחוֹת רִאשׁוֹנוֹת, דִּכְתִיב

And this is the completion of the holiness of Pesach: when the blemish of the Golden Calf is rectified, the ultimate purpose of the Exodus from Egypt is fulfilled—to merit the Giving of the Torah, the holiness of the First Tablets, as it is written
(תְּהִלִּים פ"ב, ו'):
(Tehillim 82:6):
אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי אֱלֹהִים אַתֶּם,
"I said, you are angelic beings,"
דְּלָא הֲווֹ מַיְיתֵי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
so that they would not die, as they said in Avodah Zarah
וְהָיָה בָּטֵל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, שֶׁהוּא הַשָּׂטָן, הוּא מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת, הוּא יֵצֶר הָרָע
and the evil inclination would be nullified, for "he is Satan, he is the Angel of Death, he is the evil inclination"
(בָּבָא בַּתְרָא ט"ז.).
(Bava Basra 16a).

וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי קוֹרִין בְּפֶסַח כָּל פָּרָשַׁת הַמּוֹעֲדוֹת, וּפָרָשַׁת "שׁוֹר אוֹ כֶשֶׂב" מַקְדִּימִין לָהֶם שֶׁהוּא שַׁיָּיךְ כּוּלּוֹ לְפָרָשַׁת מוֹעֲדִים, וְהַפֶּסַח שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל קְדוּשַּׁת הַמּוֹעֲדִים.

And therefore on Pesach we read the entire section of the festivals, prefaced by the section of "An ox or a sheep," which wholly pertains to the section of the festivals, since Pesach is the root of the holiness of all the festivals.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, Second Day of Pesach 14 — “This section is an introduction to all the festivals, as the Zohar, Emor, explains ‘seven days under its mother’: until one Shabbos passes over it… Then a person attains the recognition that in all things he has no power from his own side, and this recognition is truly his acquisition, so he has something to offer to Hashem. Therefore it is an introduction to all the festivals, for the festivals are ‘which you shall proclaim’: Hashem handed this power to Israel… And to the degree that a person recognizes the holiness of Shabbos, fixed and enduring from His side, so Hashem gives him power to sanctify the times.” Connection: The same reading of “an ox or a sheep” as the introduction to the festivals Israel sanctify, adding that Israel’s power to sanctify comes from the Shabbos that must first pass over the offering.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain, Shem MiShmuel, Pesach, Second Day — “On the second day of Pesach one must give a reason why we begin the day's Torah reading with the section ‘An ox or a sheep,’ though it seemingly has no connection with the section of the festivals after it. In the Midrash on Emor: ‘From that very abomination of which it is written, They made themselves a molten calf, from it bring Me an offering, as it says, An ox or a sheep or a goat; with their evil they gladden the king.’ This indicates more than atonement: the evil itself gladdens the King. This came from the great repentance Israel did, although the stumbling did not come from them but from the Mixed Multitude.” Connection: The Sochatchover asks Rav Tzadok's question about the second-day reading and gives the same key, the repair of the Calf. He adds that the sin is not only atoned for but turned into the King's joy.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Korach 13 — “The Mixed Multitude came through Moshe Rabbeinu, who accepted them, as in Shemos Rabbah 42: ‘Your people have acted corruptly’… ‘I told you not to mingle the Mixed Multitude with them; you, being humble and upright, said to Me: one always accepts penitents.’ By law he did not need to accept them, since they converted only because they saw Israel’s greatness, just as converts are not accepted in the days of Mashiach… Yet since Moshe accepted them, after the fact they were converts. Through the Mixed Multitude the leaven in the dough branched out into the heart of Israel, for at the Giving of the Torah it is written ‘I said, you are angelic beings.’” Connection: The same Midrash on Moshe’s acceptance of the Mixed Multitude and the calf, adding the halachic status of such converts and that through them the leaven entered Israel’s heart.

paragraphs.text: Bava Basra 16a — "Reish Lakish said: He is the Satan, he is the evil inclination, he is the Angel of Death." A baraisa there: "He descends and leads astray, ascends and arouses wrath, takes permission and takes the soul." Rashi: he incites a person to sin, then accuses him and receives permission to kill him.
